provenance.review: machine-checked by lab.tools.check_registry (verbatim quotes, sections, ids); content reviewed by Claude where noted in review_notes

draft_notes: Only the supplied document was used. The carriage return in the supplied requirement prefix is preserved as \r in identifiers. Referenced protocols were not supplied. The document does not specify timeout durations, the minimal bond amount, admissible parameters, or the systemic-error threshold. It does not provide a complete state-transition graph. Section 7 associates formal appeal validation with R1, whereas section 5 describes R1 as suspicion with verification initiated; their precise relationship is unspecified. The 30-DTI-Day limit is read subject to the explicit E1 exception. Provisions are separated beyond the typical count to preserve distinct classification conditions, states, obligations, and prohibitions.

requirements.title: Treat errors as system states
requirements.quote: Errors in DKP are treated as system states, not as moral failures or intent-based misconduct.
requirements.interpretation: Check that error records and handling classify errors as system states. Detecting moral or intent-based treatment requires an operational definition of those forms of treatment.
requirements.criterion: Errors are treated as system states and not as moral failures or intent-based misconduct.
requirements.gap: Observed as error records carrying states only, no blame or misconduct labels.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how records and actions are classified as moral or intent-based treatment.

requirements.title: Require procedural nonpunitive handling
requirements.quote: ERROR handling is strictly procedural and non-punitive.
requirements.interpretation: Compare handling actions with an authorized procedure and a classification of punitive actions. The document does not completely define either classification.
requirements.criterion: Every ERROR handling action is procedural and non-punitive.
requirements.gap: Procedural: §5 states in order; non-punitive: no measure sourced from the error case itself (a harsher recomputed Justice outcome is Q-021).
hypotheses_needed: Declare the authorized procedure and the test for punitive handling.

requirements.title: Respect upstream protocol ordering
requirements.quote:
- strictly downstream of DKP-0-ORACLE-001 (PTL) and DKP-0-TIME-001,
- downstream of DKP-1-IDENTITY-001, DKP-1-IMPACT-001, DKP-1-JUSTICE-001,
- downstream of all L3 protocols (INTERNAL-SEC, DEFENSE, ANTITERROR),
requirements.interpretation: Check the system dependency graph or execution trace for the stated ordering. The text does not say whether downstream means dependency precedence, execution order, or both.
requirements.criterion: ERROR operates downstream of all named upstream protocols and all L3 protocols.
requirements.gap: The meaning of downstream and complete identifiers for the L3 protocols are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether downstream constrains dependencies, execution order, or both.

requirements.title: Precede crisis protocol operation
requirements.quote: - upstream of DKP-4-CRISIS-001.
requirements.interpretation: Check ERROR's ordering relative to CRISIS in the declared protocol architecture. Upstream is not defined as a specific graph or temporal relation.
requirements.criterion: ERROR operates upstream of DKP-4-CRISIS-001.
requirements.gap: The operational meaning of upstream is unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the dependency or execution relation represented by upstream.

requirements.title: Prohibit new coercive measures
requirements.quote: - DKP-4-ERROR-001 SHALL NOT introduce new coercive measures.
requirements.interpretation: Compare measures introduced by ERROR with an existing-measures baseline and a coercion classification. Neither the baseline nor the classification is defined here.
requirements.criterion: No new measure introduced by ERROR is coercive.
requirements.gap: The baseline for new measures and the definition of coercive measures are missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the baseline and operational classification of coercive measures.

requirements.title: Prohibit axiom and truth reinterpretation
requirements.quote: - DKP-4-ERROR-001 SHALL NOT reinterpret axioms or Physical Truth.
requirements.interpretation: Compare ERROR actions with authoritative axiom and Physical Truth representations. A check needs a distinction between prohibited reinterpretation and permitted correction of an E1 error.
requirements.criterion: ERROR does not reinterpret axioms or Physical Truth.
requirements.gap: Observed as measurements written by a source other than PTL; axiom reinterpretation is not modelled beyond that.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how reinterpretation differs from correcting a measurement or oracle error.

requirements.title: Restrict intervention in Justice outcomes
requirements.quote: - DKP-4-ERROR-001 SHALL NOT override Justice outcomes, only request recomputation.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect ERROR operations affecting Justice outcomes. They must be recomputation requests rather than direct outcome overrides.
requirements.criterion: Every ERROR intervention in a Justice outcome is a request for recomputation, and none is an override.

requirements.title: Define qualifying system errors
requirements.quote: An Error is any PTL-confirmed deviation between:
requirements.interpretation: Check PTL confirmation, a deviation involving intended behavior, execution, or recorded state, and at least one listed incorrect result. The phrase between followed by or does not specify exactly which comparisons are required.
requirements.criterion: An Error is a PTL-confirmed deviation involving intended protocol behavior, actual execution, or recorded state that results in incorrect restriction or action, attribution, impact calculation, or application of protocol rules.
requirements.gap: The required comparison relation and the standards for incorrect results are not fully specified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which comparisons establish a deviation and which specifications determine correctness.

requirements.title: Define decisions eligible for appeal
requirements.quote:
- affects a Subject’s rights, access, assets, or status,
- is derived from protocol execution,
- is not explicitly marked as irreversible by higher-layer rules.
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate all three conditions on a DKP action or outcome. Eligibility depends on supplied impact metadata, protocol provenance, and explicit higher-layer irreversibility markings.
requirements.criterion: A DKP action or outcome is appealable if it affects a Subject's rights, access, assets, or status, derives from protocol execution, and is not explicitly marked irreversible by higher-layer rules.
requirements.gap: 'Marked irreversible by a higher-layer rule' is a declared flag.

requirements.title: Define qualifying formal appellants
requirements.quote:
- is directly affected by an Appealable Decision, and
- submits a formal error claim under this protocol.
requirements.interpretation: A Subject qualifies only when directly affected by an appealable decision and submitting a formal claim. The direct-effect relationship must be supplied because the document gives no attribution test for it.
requirements.criterion: An Appellant is a Subject directly affected by an Appealable Decision who submits a formal error claim under this protocol.
requirements.gap: The document does not define how to establish that a Subject is directly affected. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the test for a direct effect on a Subject.

requirements.title: Classify measurement and oracle errors
requirements.quote:
- E1 – Measurement Error

  PTL sensor, data ingestion, or oracle misreporting.
requirements.interpretation: Assign E1 to the specified measurement-related errors. The wording leaves open whether PTL sensor and data ingestion refer to any malfunction or specifically misreporting.
requirements.criterion: E1 covers PTL sensor, data ingestion, or oracle misreporting errors.
requirements.gap: The exact qualifying sensor and ingestion behaviors are not defined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether misreporting qualifies all three sources or only oracle errors.

requirements.title: Classify incorrect protocol execution
requirements.quote:
- E2 – Execution Error

  Protocol logic executed incorrectly or out of order.
requirements.interpretation: Compare execution traces with the protocol's logic and required ordering. Either incorrect logic execution or an ordering violation qualifies as E2.
requirements.criterion: E2 applies when protocol logic executes incorrectly or out of order.
requirements.gap: The applicable logic and ordering specifications are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the protocol specification used as the execution reference.

requirements.title: Classify incorrect identity attribution
requirements.quote:
- E3 – Attribution Error

  Incorrect Identity binding or responsibility assignment.
requirements.interpretation: Compare Identity bindings and responsibility assignments with their correctness criteria. Either kind of incorrect assignment qualifies as E3.
requirements.criterion: E3 applies when an Identity binding or responsibility assignment is incorrect.
requirements.gap: Correct binding and responsibility-assignment criteria are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the reference used to establish attribution correctness.

requirements.title: Classify incorrect impact computations
requirements.quote:
- E4 – Impact Computation Error

  Incorrect impact magnitude, scope, or channel mapping.
requirements.interpretation: Compare impact outputs with an authoritative computation. An incorrect magnitude, scope, or channel mapping qualifies as E4.
requirements.criterion: E4 applies when impact magnitude, scope, or channel mapping is incorrect.
requirements.gap: The impact computation and mapping rules needed to establish correctness are absent. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the reference computation and mapping rules.

requirements.title: Classify procedural rule violations
requirements.quote:
- E5 – Procedural Error

  Violation of timing (DTI), escalation rules, or isolation constraints.
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate execution against applicable timing, escalation, and isolation requirements. A violation in any of these categories qualifies as E5.
requirements.criterion: E5 applies when timing, escalation rules, or isolation constraints are violated.
requirements.gap: The complete applicable procedural rules are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the applicable timing, escalation, and isolation requirements.

requirements.title: Define normal operating state
requirements.quote:
- R0 – No Error

  * System operating within admissible parameters.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a system labeled R0 operates within its admissible parameters. The document does not supply those parameters.
requirements.criterion: R0 denotes system operation within admissible parameters.
requirements.gap: Admissible parameters and their bounds are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare admissible parameters and any associated bounds.

requirements.title: Define suspected error state
requirements.quote:
- R1 – Error Suspected

  * Error signal detected; non-coercive verification initiated.
requirements.interpretation: Check that R1 records contain a detected error signal and initiation of non-coercive verification. The verification action requires a supplied coercion classification.
requirements.criterion: R1 denotes a detected error signal with non-coercive verification initiated.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which verification actions qualify as non-coercive.

requirements.title: Define confirmed error state
requirements.quote:
- R2 – Error Confirmed

  * Error validated via PTL and protocol audit.
requirements.interpretation: Check that an R2 designation has both PTL validation and protocol-audit validation. This tests recorded validation status rather than independently establishing its correctness.
requirements.criterion: R2 requires error validation via both PTL and protocol audit.
requirements.gap: Verification of E2, E4, E5 is declared on input; E1 and E3 are modelled.

requirements.title: Define applied correction state
requirements.quote:
- R3 – Correction Applied

  * Corrective action executed.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a case labeled R3 has an executed corrective action. The state description does not itself require appeal resolution.
requirements.criterion: R3 requires execution of corrective action.

requirements.title: Define residual dispute state
requirements.quote:
- R4 – Residual Dispute

  * Correction completed, but appeal unresolved.
requirements.interpretation: Check that R4 has both completed correction and an unresolved appeal. The text does not specify a priority rule for overlapping R3 and R4 conditions.
requirements.criterion: R4 requires completed correction and an unresolved appeal.

requirements.title: Index states and enforce timeouts
requirements.quote: All states are indexed by DTI-Day and subject to timeouts.
requirements.interpretation: Require a DTI-Day index and an applicable timeout for every state. Timeout durations, starting events, and expiry consequences are not specified, including for R0.
requirements.criterion: Every state has a DTI-Day index and is governed by a timeout.
requirements.gap: Timeout durations, clocks, and expiry behavior are missing. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare timeout durations, start events, and expiry behavior for every state.

requirements.title: Authorize review initiation pathways
requirements.quote:
- PTL-detected inconsistency,
- internal protocol audit,
- formal appeal submission by an Appellant accompanied by a minimal economic bond.
requirements.interpretation: Recognize the three permitted initiation pathways and require a minimal economic bond for the formal-appeal pathway. MAY does not require every trigger to start a review, and the wording does not expressly declare the list exhaustive.
requirements.criterion: Review may start from a PTL inconsistency, internal audit, or formal Appellant appeal accompanied by a minimal economic bond.
requirements.gap: The minimal bond amount or determination rule is not defined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the minimal bond rule and whether the listed initiation pathways are exhaustive.

requirements.title: Refund bonds for confirmed errors
requirements.quote: The bond SHALL be returned in full if the error is confirmed (R2).
requirements.interpretation: For a bonded appeal whose error reaches R2, check that the full bond is returned. The amount condition is explicit, but no refund deadline is given.
requirements.criterion: If the error is confirmed in R2, the entire bond is returned.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a settlement point or observation window for evaluating refund completion.

requirements.title: Allocate unfounded appeal bonds
requirements.quote: If the appeal is rejected as unfounded, the bond SHALL be used to cover system audit costs.
requirements.interpretation: Check the disposition of a bond after rejection as unfounded. The text does not specify treatment of a surplus, audit costs exceeding the bond, or procedural rejection without an unfounded finding.
requirements.criterion: A bond associated with an appeal rejected as unfounded is used to cover system audit costs.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether the entire bond is allocated to audit costs or only the amount needed to cover those costs.

requirements.title: Prohibit prediction and intent inference
requirements.quote: No prediction or intent inference is permitted.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect review inputs and operations for prediction or intent inference. The text does not delimit whether this prohibition applies specifically to initiation or to all ERROR handling.
requirements.criterion: No operation within the applicable scope performs prediction or intent inference.
requirements.gap: Observed as explicit inference or prediction records.
hypotheses_needed: Declare prediction and intent-inference classifications and whether the prohibition applies to initiation or all handling.

requirements.title: Require structured appeal submission fields
requirements.quote:
- reference the specific Appealable Decision,
- include PTL-indexed evidence or pointers,
- be submitted within 30 DTI-Days from the moment the decision was recorded in PTL,
requirements.interpretation: Validate that an appeal references a specific appealable decision, contains PTL-indexed evidence or pointers, and specifies an alleged category E1–E5. The timing requirement in the excerpt is checked separately.
requirements.criterion: The appeal identifies a specific Appealable Decision, includes PTL-indexed evidence or pointers, and specifies an alleged category in E1–E5.

requirements.title: Enforce ordinary appeal filing deadline
requirements.quote: - be submitted within 30 DTI-Days from the moment the decision was recorded in PTL,
requirements.interpretation: Compare submission time with the decision's PTL recording time using DTI-Day elapsed time. Read with the following E1 exemption, ordinary appeals must arrive no later than 30 DTI-Days after recording.
requirements.criterion: For appeals outside the E1 exception, submission occurs within 30 DTI-Days after PTL recording of the decision.

requirements.title: Exempt oracle errors from limitations
requirements.quote: Errors of category E1 (Oracle / Physical Truth error) are not subject to any statute of limitations.
requirements.interpretation: Ensure an E1 error is not time-barred. The document does not say whether alleging E1 suffices for exemption or whether the category must first be validated.
requirements.criterion: Errors qualifying as E1 are not rejected or barred because a limitations period has elapsed.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether an E1 allegation or a validated E1 classification activates the exemption.

requirements.title: Bound optional contested decision suspension
requirements.quote: Upon formal validation of an appeal (state R1), execution of the contested decision, if reversible, MAY be temporarily suspended for up to 7 DTI-Days (Status Quo Suspension) pending verification.
requirements.interpretation: If this optional suspension is used, check formal validation in R1, decision reversibility, pending verification, and a duration no greater than 7 DTI-Days. The text does not specify how reversibility is established or whether repeated suspensions are permitted.
requirements.criterion: A Status Quo Suspension follows formal appeal validation in R1, concerns a reversible decision, remains pending verification, and lasts at most 7 DTI-Days.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how reversibility is determined and whether the seven-day cap applies per suspension or cumulatively.

requirements.title: Reject formally deficient appeals procedurally
requirements.quote: Appeals that do not meet formal requirements SHALL be rejected procedurally, without prejudice.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a formally deficient appeal receives a procedural rejection without prejudice. The phrase without prejudice requires a declared effect on future filings and substantive review.
requirements.criterion: Failure to meet formal requirements results in procedural rejection without prejudice.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the effects of without-prejudice rejection on refiling and substantive adjudication.

requirements.title: Recompute outputs after error confirmation
requirements.quote:
Upon confirmation of an error:

- affected protocol outputs SHALL be recomputed,
requirements.interpretation: For a confirmed error, identify affected protocol outputs and verify recomputation. The document does not define the affected-output dependency boundary or a completion deadline.
requirements.criterion: Confirmation of an error requires recomputation of all affected protocol outputs.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how affected outputs are identified and when recomputation completion is evaluated.

requirements.title: Roll back reversible error effects
requirements.quote: - reversible effects SHALL be rolled back,
requirements.interpretation: Following error confirmation, verify rollback of effects classified as reversible. Classification and successful rollback require an effect model and a restoration reference.
requirements.criterion: Upon error confirmation, reversible effects are rolled back.
requirements.gap: Enforcement measures are treated as reversible unless declared otherwise.
hypotheses_needed: Declare reversibility and successful restoration criteria and the rollback evaluation horizon.

requirements.title: Record and compensate irreversible effects
requirements.quote: - irreversible effects SHALL be logged and compensated where possible,
requirements.interpretation: Following confirmation, require logs for irreversible effects and compensation when feasible. Logging is directly testable; feasibility and adequate compensation need additional rules.
requirements.criterion: Irreversible effects are logged and, where compensation is possible, compensated.
requirements.gap: Compensation amounts are not defined; only the log entry is checked.
hypotheses_needed: Declare compensation feasibility, adequacy, and completion criteria.

requirements.title: Permit Justice reinvocation with corrections
requirements.quote: - Justice MAY be re-invoked using corrected inputs.
requirements.interpretation: Following confirmation, Justice reinvocation is optional. When exercised under this clause, inspect input provenance to verify use of corrected inputs.
requirements.criterion: An optional Justice reinvocation following error confirmation uses corrected inputs.

requirements.title: Prohibit penalties introduced by handling
requirements.quote: ERROR handling never introduces new penalties.
requirements.interpretation: Compare penalties attributable to ERROR handling with the preceding penalty state. A supplied penalty classification is needed to distinguish penalties from other effects.
requirements.criterion: ERROR handling introduces no new penalties.
requirements.gap: A harsher recomputed outcome gives UNKNOWN (open question Q-021).
hypotheses_needed: Declare the penalty classification and comparison baseline.

requirements.title: Minimize correction secondary impact
requirements.quote:
All corrections MUST:

- minimize secondary impact,
requirements.interpretation: Compare a correction's secondary impact with feasible alternatives using a declared impact model. The text supplies neither an objective function nor the set of alternatives.
requirements.criterion: The correction minimizes secondary impact.
requirements.gap: The secondary-impact measure and feasible comparison set are undefined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the secondary-impact objective, evaluation horizon, and feasible alternatives.

requirements.title: Preserve truth ledger consistency
requirements.quote: - preserve PTL consistency,
requirements.interpretation: Evaluate PTL consistency before and after each correction and, if required by the consistency model, during execution. The document does not state the relevant PTL invariants.
requirements.criterion: Every correction preserves PTL consistency.
requirements.gap: PTL consistency rules and their temporal scope are not supplied. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the PTL consistency invariant and whether intermediate states must satisfy it.

requirements.title: Prefer reversal over compensation
requirements.quote: - prefer reversibility over compensation,
requirements.interpretation: Check the choice among available corrections for preference toward reversal. The wording does not specify whether this is an absolute priority or a preference that can be outweighed by other principles.
requirements.criterion: Correction selection prefers reversibility over compensation.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether reversal has absolute priority or a defeasible preference.

requirements.title: Avoid cascades beyond error scope
requirements.quote: - avoid cascading changes outside the error scope.
requirements.interpretation: Trace changes caused by a correction and compare their scope with the error boundary. The text does not define the scope boundary or whether avoid requires zero external cascading changes or a best-effort choice.
requirements.criterion: Corrections avoid cascading changes outside the error scope.
requirements.gap: Error scope, cascade identification, and the strictness of avoid are undefined. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the error boundary, cascade model, and whether avoidance is absolute or best effort.

requirements.title: Automatically escalate systemic error detection
requirements.quote: If a systemic or cascading error is detected (impacting more than a protocol-defined threshold of Subjects or cross-layer execution), DKP-4-ERROR-001 SHALL automatically escalate to DKP-4-CRISIS-001 for Systemic Rollback and coordinated recovery.
requirements.interpretation: Check automatic escalation when the affected-Subject count exceeds the protocol-defined threshold or cross-layer execution is affected. The parenthetical could instead mean that a protocol-defined threshold also applies to cross-layer effects; the text does not resolve this.
requirements.criterion: Detection of a systemic or cascading error triggers automatic escalation to DKP-4-CRISIS-001 for Systemic Rollback and coordinated recovery; the Subject-count condition uses strictly more than the protocol-defined threshold.
requirements.gap: 'Protocol-defined threshold' of affected Subjects is not modelled; the cascade is a declared window.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the threshold source, cross-layer trigger interpretation, and timing criterion for automatic escalation.

requirements.title: Anchor and date error case logs
requirements.quote:
All error cases MUST be:

- logged with PTL anchoring,
requirements.interpretation: For every error case, check for a log with a PTL anchor and a DTI-Day index, as required by the following indexing bullet. The text does not prescribe a record serialization.
requirements.criterion: Every error case is logged with PTL anchoring and indexed by DTI-Day.

requirements.title: Enable retrospective error case review
requirements.quote: - reviewable post-factum,
requirements.interpretation: Test whether error cases can be retrieved and reviewed after the events. The document does not define authorized reviewers, retention duration, or the information necessary for review.
requirements.criterion: Every error case remains reviewable post-factum.
requirements.gap: Review access, required review information, and retention duration are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare who can review cases, the necessary information, and the retention horizon.

requirements.title: Include cases in reliability metrics
requirements.quote: - included in system reliability metrics.
requirements.interpretation: Reconcile the error case inventory with the cases contributing to reliability metrics. The document does not supply metric definitions or inclusion timing.
requirements.criterion: Every error case is included in system reliability metrics.
requirements.gap: Metric computation rules and the reporting period for inclusion are absent. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the metric contribution rule and reporting period.

requirements.title: Prohibit suppression of valid appeals
requirements.quote:
This protocol SHALL NOT:

- suppress valid appeals,
requirements.interpretation: Compare valid appeal submissions with intake and processing records to detect suppression. The text does not define suppression or whether validity means formal sufficiency or a substantively founded claim.
requirements.criterion: The protocol does not suppress valid appeals.
hypotheses_needed: Declare whether validity is formal or substantive and which acts or omissions constitute suppression.

requirements.title: Prohibit retaliation against appellants
requirements.quote: - retaliate against Appellants,
requirements.interpretation: Inspect actions affecting Appellants for a prohibited retaliatory relationship to their appeals. The text supplies no observable test for retaliation.
requirements.criterion: The protocol does not retaliate against Appellants.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a retaliation criterion consistent with the prohibition on intent inference.

requirements.title: Prohibit hiding error statistics
requirements.quote: - hide error statistics,
requirements.interpretation: Compare available error statistics with stored statistics and access rules. The prohibition does not identify an audience or a required publication schedule.
requirements.criterion: The protocol does not hide error statistics.
requirements.gap: The required audience, disclosure scope, and meaning of hiding are unspecified. No lab check implemented yet.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the visibility obligations used to identify hidden statistics.

requirements.title: Prohibit discretionary protocol overrides
requirements.quote: - introduce discretionary overrides.
requirements.interpretation: Inspect changes and execution paths for overrides based on discretion. A check requires a definition distinguishing discretionary overrides from authorized procedural decisions.
requirements.criterion: The protocol introduces no discretionary overrides.
hypotheses_needed: Declare the distinction between discretionary overrides and authorized procedural actions.

requirements.title: Require controlled protocol change procedure
requirements.quote: This protocol is changed only through the controlled procedure of DKP-4-UPGRADE-001: proposal, simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001, acceptance conditions, activation window and rollback.
requirements.interpretation: For normative changes, verify evidence of the named controlled procedure, including mandatory simulation and audit. The presentation-only exception is checked separately; the referenced documents are needed to determine acceptance, activation, rollback, and whether rollback means capability or actual execution.
requirements.criterion: A normative protocol change follows DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 with proposal, simulation under DKP-8-SIMULATION-001, audit under DKP-8-AUDIT-001, acceptance conditions, activation window, and rollback.
requirements.gap: Declared stages of the change; the procedure itself is upgrade_lifecycle.
hypotheses_needed: Declare surrogate procedural criteria if simulating without the referenced documents, including the meaning of rollback.

requirements.title: Assign modified protocols new identifiers
requirements.quote: - modifications require a new protocol identifier,
requirements.interpretation: Compare the protocol identifier before and after a normative modification. Read with the presentation-only exception, changes without normative effects do not trigger this requirement.
requirements.criterion: A modification subject to upgrade requirements receives a new protocol identifier.
hypotheses_needed: Declare how normative changes are identified and whether new means changed from the prior identifier or globally unused.

requirements.title: Require explicit compatibility declaration
requirements.quote: - explicit compatibility declaration.
requirements.interpretation: For modifications subject to upgrade requirements, check that an explicit compatibility declaration is present. The document does not prescribe its fields or compatibility targets.
requirements.criterion: Every modification subject to upgrade requirements includes an explicit compatibility declaration.
requirements.gap: No target named (F-041): FAIL without a declaration, UNKNOWN otherwise.

requirements.title: Handle presentation corrections by date
requirements.quote: Presentation-only corrections that do not change normative content are not Upgrades (DKP-4-UPGRADE-001 §3); they are recorded only by the "Last updated" date of this document.
requirements.interpretation: Check that a correction with unchanged normative content is not classified as an Upgrade and uses only the Last updated date as its change record. The text does not define normative equivalence or explain whether the front-matter last_updated key is the intended date field.
requirements.criterion: Presentation-only corrections preserving normative content are not Upgrades and are recorded only through the document's Last updated date.
hypotheses_needed: Declare a normative-equivalence test and map Last updated to the document's date metadata.

requirements.title: Publish canonical edition integrity digests
requirements.quote: Edition integrity: the SHA-256 digest of the canonical source of each published edition is listed in `SHA256SUMS.txt` of the canonical repository (github.com/anahronic/World).
requirements.interpretation: For each published edition, compute SHA-256 over its canonical source and compare it with the corresponding repository manifest entry. The text does not identify source files, byte canonicalization rules, or the mapping from editions to entries.
requirements.criterion: Every published edition has its canonical-source SHA-256 digest correctly listed in SHA256SUMS.txt in github.com/anahronic/World.
requirements.gap: Checked on the pinned commit and on simulated releases, not on the published site.
hypotheses_needed: Declare which exact source bytes and manifest entry correspond to each published edition.
